name: Fault-equivalent identity removal
summary: Adding or removing a phase-free two-legged spider on a wire is fault-equivalent.
description:
The ordinary [identity removal](../identity-removal/) rule is fault-equivalent: a wire may be split by a phase-free Z-spider, or the spider removed again, without changing which faults are possible. Fault equivalence is with respect to *edge-flip noise*: every edge of the diagram can suffer a Pauli $X$, $Y$ or $Z$ flip of weight 1. A flip on the bare wire corresponds to the same flip on either of the two edges, and flips $P_1$, $P_2$ on the two edges correspond to the flip $P_1P_2$ on the wire, which has at most the same weight.

The rule was introduced as the distance-preserving rewrite $(r_{\text{elim}})$; distance-preserving rewrites were later shown to be exactly the fault-equivalent rewrites. In the complete axiomatisation of fault equivalence of Rüsch, Rodatz and Kissinger, $(\textsc{Elim}_{\text{fe}})$ is the weighted version: the noisy wire with weight $\vec w$ equals the spider with a noisy edge of weight $\vec w$ on one side and a fault-free edge on the other.
